### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb`.

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 46 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a426d6f07172e436350b9ef71eb5865d34d9069a` — the merge of head `88e7099e59ac0bcee82457a1bf091251cd4ece82` into base `199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a426d6f07172e436350b9ef71eb5865d34d9069a && git checkout a426d6f07172e436350b9ef71eb5865d34d9069a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb 88e7099e59ac0bcee82457a1bf091251cd4ece82 && git checkout -B drift-repro 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb && git merge --no-ff 88e7099e59ac0bcee82457a1bf091251cd4ece82

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a10e98535fc97cf953c32fc96392640c107a5318`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/scim-sso-adoption.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-account-at-proven-domain.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-provider-lifecycle.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-provider-lifecycle.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts (read only)

### ① Derived judgments

- **One parse (#32975).** `ssoDomainEntryHost` is the former `provenEntryHost`, exported unchanged in body; `ssoProviderProvenDomains` now delegates to `ssoDomainEntryHosts` with identical semantics (skip non-accepted entries, dedupe). `scim-sso-adoption.ts` drops its own split/lowercase parse and its `emailDomain` and reads both sides through the shared parse (`ssoAddressDomain`, `ssoDomainEntryHosts`), so SCIM and the account rule agree on every entry/address pair (14×5 agreement table pinned). Directions: narrowed (an entry or address that only folds into a host — full-width letters, URL/port/path shapes — no longer vouches for SCIM adoption) and widened (root dot, Unicode/punycode read as one domain, as the account rule already did). Both are declared. The `null` vs `undefined` switch at the `vouching` line is consistent with `ssoAddressDomain`'s return.
- **Register/edit refusal (#32960).** `ssoDomainEntryNotBare` runs in `assertSsoProviderDomainFree` after `ssoDomainTooLong` and before the claim rule, only on `/sso/register` and `/sso/update-provider` with a non-blank `domain` from a caller with a session; blanks skipped like every list parse. The bridges (`/admin/sso/register`, `register-saml`, `/admin/sso/update-provider`) re-dispatch through those paths, pinned for the direct door and the SAML bridge. The generic data layer for `sys_sso_provider` is read-only (`enable.apiMethods`), so no other write path stores `domain`. The console's edit actions (`edit_oidc_provider`, `edit_saml_provider`, toggles) send no `domain`, so an existing provider holding a URL entry stays editable for its other fields; nothing pre-existing is newly blocked from the console.
- Claim rule (`providerDomains`, WHATWG host parse) untouched; with the shape refusal in front, every newly storable entry reads the same under both (pinned). A legacy URL entry of another provider still blocks a collision: refuses more, never less. Red line held.
- nit N1: the docs and changeset say "edit the provider's domain to the bare host names", but no console action edits `domain`; the only door is `POST /api/v1/auth/sso/update-provider` (or the admin bridge) with `domain`. Name the door in both so an operator can act.
- nit N2 (follow-up, not here): a provider saved before this rule with a URL entry now silently "names no domain" for SCIM adoption too. A one-time boot or Setup warning naming such providers would make the narrowing visible; a p3 loose-ends card at most.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch` with `fix(plugin-auth)!` and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (with its widened arm stated) matches the repo's convention for a runtime refusal at an auth door; no schema key, column or published type moves. New exports are module-level in `sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts` (not a published subpath change). `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right: stored rows are not rewritten. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. `Skills-docs: none — REASON` acceptable.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Security boundary: SSO account creation and SCIM adoption; both moves fail closed except the declared one-spelling widening, which only matches what the account rule already accepted.
- Author login `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); implemented by area A1 session_016WV4d1NJYFGVi2FRztyBNo.
- CI at this head: 29 green, 8 in progress, none red when read (15:22Z). The ACCEPT must re-read checks.

### ④ Design judgment

Refusing the shape at the write door is the right place: an entry that passes the vendor's DNS check and then proves nothing at sign-in is a silent misconfiguration, and the 400 names the entry and the accepted form. Sharing one parse across the account rule and SCIM removes the three-readings divergence the card describes. Not rewriting stored rows is the conservative choice and is stated. Holds against the cited code and both cards' scenarios.
